summary: Linux is a family of open-source Unix-like operating systems based on the Linux kernel.
body_text: Linux is a family of open-source Unix-like operating systems based on the Linux kernel. It is typically packaged with other software into Linux distributions. Linux is widely used on servers, desktops, and embedded devices.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Linux is a family of open-source Unix-like operating systems based on the Linux kernel. Linux distributions combine the kernel with package managers, libraries, and user-facing tools.

sections.title: Usage
sections.content: Linux is widely used in servers, cloud infrastructure, embedded devices, and developer workstations. Distributions vary, but they typically include a package manager and a configurable shell environment.

summary: Arch Linux is an independently developed x86-64 general-purpose Linux distribution.
body_text: Arch Linux is an independently developed x86-64 general-purpose Linux distribution that strives for simplicity, modernity, pragmatism, user centrality, and versatility. It uses a rolling release model and the pacman package manager.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Arch Linux is an independently developed x86-64 general-purpose Linux distribution. It follows a rolling release model rather than fixed major releases.

sections.title: Package management
sections.content: Arch Linux uses the pacman package manager for installing, updating, and removing software packages from official repositories.

summary: Pacman is the package manager used by Arch Linux.
body_text: Pacman is the package manager used by Arch Linux. It can install, upgrade, configure, and remove packages. Pacman synchronizes package databases and supports system upgrades with pacman -Syu.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Pacman is the package manager used by Arch Linux. It synchronizes package databases and performs system upgrades.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
To refresh package databases and upgrade the system, run ```text
pacman -Syu
```.

summary: systemd is the system and service manager used on Arch Linux.
body_text: systemd is the system and service manager used on Arch Linux. It manages units such as services, sockets, mounts, and timers. The systemctl command is used to inspect and control systemd units.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: systemd is the system and service manager used on Arch Linux. It manages services, timers, mounts, sockets, and other units.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
To start a service immediately and enable it at boot, use ```text
systemctl enable --now sshd.service
```.
